bib.title: W2V-BERT: Combining Contrastive Learning and Masked Language Modeling for Self-Supervised Speech Pre-Training
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv:2108.06209v2; PDF does not print a venue)

question: Can masked-language-model style prediction over learned discrete speech tokens be trained end to end together with wav2vec 2.0's contrastive task, and does it beat contrastive-only pre-training for ASR?
hypothesis: Combining a contrastive task (which yields a discriminative codebook) with a masked prediction task over its token IDs gives better speech representations than contrastive learning alone, and avoids HuBERT's iterative re-clustering.
contributions: Propose w2v-BERT, optimizing contrastive and masked prediction losses simultaneously end to end.
Large gain on a real-world voice search task over conformer wav2vec 2.0.
Analysis showing the contrastive module is necessary for masked prediction, and that masked prediction helps with easy negatives.

method.summary: A conformer feature encoder, a contrastive module (quantizer + conformer stack, wav2vec 2.0 task) and a masked prediction module (conformer stack with softmax over quantizer token IDs) are pre-trained jointly on unlabeled speech with Lp = beta*Lc + gamma*Lm. The pre-trained encoder is then fine-tuned with an LSTM decoder as a sequence transducer on LibriSpeech or Voice Search.
method.task: self-supervised speech pre-training, then ASR fine-tuning

datasets.name: LibriSpeech 960hr
datasets.split: eval on dev-clean, dev-other, test-clean, test-other
datasets.preprocessing: 1024-token WordPiece model built from training transcripts

datasets.name: Google Voice Search (pre-training)
datasets.source: derived from Li et al. 2021 [42]; internal

models.name: w2v-BERT XL
models.architecture: conv subsampling + 12 contrastive conformer blocks + 12 masked conformer blocks

models.name: w2v-BERT XXL
models.architecture: as XL but 30 masked conformer blocks

models.name: ASR network
models.architecture: sequence transducer: pre-trained w2v-BERT + linear (Swish, batch norm) projection + 2-layer LSTM decoder, hidden 640

models.name: w2v-Conformer XL/XXL
models.architecture: conformer, contrastive-only, linear layer instead of quantizer

training.objective: Lp = beta*Lc + gamma*Lm, Lc = Lw + alpha*Ld (contrastive + codebook diversity), Lm = cross-entropy on quantizer token IDs at masked positions; beta = gamma = 1, alpha = 0.1
training.optimizer: XL: Adam with transformer schedule; XXL: Adafactor beta1=0.9 beta2=0.98 (pre-training); fine-tune same families
training.lr: pre-train peak 2e-3; fine-tune XL encoder peak 3e-4, decoder peak 1e-3
training.steps: fine-tune from checkpoints at 400k pre-training steps; total pre-training steps not stated
training.regularisation: SpecAugment, Noisy Student Training self-training, LM fusion (where used), following Zhang et al. 2020 [21]; mask start prob 0.065, span 10, masked frames replaced by random vectors

other.XXL fine-tune optimizer: Adafactor same configuration as pre-training; encoder/decoder schedules same as XL
other.note: batch size and peak lr for XXL pre-training not stated separately; hyperparameters taken from [21] unchanged

inference.decoding: sequence transducer; LM fusion in some rows, details deferred to [21]
inference.samples: single reported number per cell; no seeds or runs stated

eval.protocol: LibriSpeech dev, dev-other, test, test-other under four settings (scratch, self-training only, pre-training only, pre-training + self-training), each with and without LM; single run, no significance test; baselines quoted from literature

limits: All hyperparameters copied from Zhang et al. [21] without tuning; authors plan to search the best configuration (Sec 6).
Voice Search data and test set are internal; no code or weights stated.
Baselines are quoted from the literature, not rerun; wav2vec 2.0 and w2v-BERT differ in model and LM size (authors compare sums).
Single runs, no seeds or significance; no compute, hardware or total pre-training steps stated.
English only; the contrastive module needed a less aggressive subsampling (3 stacked frames) on voice search, and contrastive-only baseline needed tuning.
The collapse explanation for the no-contrastive case is a hypothesis supported by training curves, not a controlled proof.
